name: Phulkopir Roast
steps: Cut cauliflower into large even florets and potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Dry the cauliflower thoroughly, then toss both vegetables with 2 g turmeric and 3 g salt.

Heat 35 ml mustard oil until shimmering, then lower to medium heat. Shallow-fry cauliflower in batches until golden at the edges, about 6 minutes per batch; lift out. Fry potatoes until lightly browned and remove.
Add the remaining oil and soften onion for 7–8 minutes. Stir in ginger, tomato, cumin, coriander, chilli and remaining turmeric; cook until the tomato collapses and oil begins to separate.

Lower the heat and whisk yogurt into the masala a spoonful at a time to prevent splitting. Add 120 ml water and remaining 7 g salt, return the fried potato and cauliflower, cover and simmer 10–12 minutes until potato is tender and sauce is thick.
Uncover and cook 3–4 minutes more, gently turning the cauliflower to coat each floret without breaking it. Sprinkle garam masala, rest 5 minutes, and serve with luchi or rice.
tips: Keep the cauliflower florets large and pre-fry them; this preserves their shape in the rich Bengali masala.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
